title: DANN: Diffractive Acoustic Neural Network for in-sensor computing system target at multi-biomarker diagnosis
problem: Deploying diffractive neural networks on integrated acoustic (surface acoustic wave) systems for analog edge AI is challenging due to hardware optimization constraints and training complexity. Existing diffractive DNN implementations focus on optical systems; acoustic realizations require novel training and optimization methods.
motivation: Acoustic in-sensor computing offers superior energy efficiency for edge AI (66% savings vs. digital circuits) and enables real-time biomarker diagnosis at the point-of-care. Analog wave-based computation avoids expensive digital signal processing.
method: The work applies diffractive neural network algorithms to surface acoustic wave (SAW) systems and introduces a co-training methodology combining Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations with gradient-descent optimization. This balances physical realism (FEA) with training efficiency (backprop) to learn diffractive patterns optimized for SAW hardware.
key_novelty: First demonstration of diffractive neural networks on integrated surface acoustic wave systems, enabled by novel FEA-gradient co-training methodology.
contributions: Novel co-training method integrating FEA simulation with gradient descent for diffractive network optimization
Validation on Major Depressive Disorder (74.07% accuracy) and prostate cancer (86.0% accuracy) diagnosis tasks
66% energy reduction compared to traditional digital approaches via in-sensor computing architecture
Proof-of-concept for analog wave physics-based edge AI beyond optical diffractive systems
limitations: Evaluation limited to two biomarker detection tasks; generalization to other acoustic sensing modalities and scalability to larger networks not discussed.
primary_theme: Acoustic diffractive neural networks for analog in-sensor biomarker diagnosis
